page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Managed through the KVM hypervisor, the instance is powered by custom Alibaba YiTian710 processors operating at a nominal clock speed of 2.75 GHz. It provisions 64 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

Hardware resource distribution excludes discrete GPU accelerators as well as local disk volumes, requiring users to rely on network-attached storage for the root filesystem and persistent application data. Baseline networking throughput is provisioned at 32 Gbps, supporting significant data transfer rates across cloud network fabrics. Because the processor utilizes the arm64 architecture, x86 instruction extensions such as AVX are not present.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides a resource configuration suited for workloads where memory capacity is the primary constraint. This hardware balance makes the instance applicable for hosting large in-memory caching platforms, enterprise in-memory databases, big data analytics engines, and high-concurrency memory-bound microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.16xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance featuring Alibaba YiTian710 processors clocked at 2.75 GHz. Hosted on a KVM hypervisor, this server provides 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware setup includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware acceleration, instead relying on network-attached storage for disk volume needs. It provides a baseline network throughput of 32 Gbps. With its high memory-to-core density and dedicated ARM compute allocations, the instance is structured to deliver resource-efficient capacity for memory-intensive production workloads. It is suited for applications such as in-memory databases, large-scale Redis and Memcached clusters, data caching tiers, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines requiring high RAM capacity per virtual CPU core.
